{{nihongo|'''Aburahi Shrine'''|油日神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

'''Aburahi Shrine''' (あぶらひじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}, {{ill|Kōka, Shiga|Q847584|qid=Q847584}}, {{ill|Aburahi, Kōka Town|Q86737182|qid=Q86737182}}. It is a {{ill|Kokushi genzaisha|Q118304363|qid=Q118304363}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}. The enshrined deity, Aburahi Ōkami, was revered by {{ill|bushi|Q1975935|qid=Q1975935}} as a god of victory, and from the shrine’s name was also worshipped as a god of the fire of oil. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mount Aburahi}} is regarded as the {{ill|Sacred mountains|Q1595289|qid=Q1595289}}, and at its summit stands Take Shrine, which enshrines the goddess Mizuhanome. The shrine crest is a {{ill|Papaya (disambiguation)|Q3894703|qid=Q3894703}} combined with a {{ill|Hikiryō mon|Q11487136|qid=Q11487136|lt=double-bar design}}.

=== History ===
The date of the shrine’s founding is unknown, but it is traditionally said to have been established during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yōmei|Q349281|qid=Q349281}} or {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}. According to legend, the name “Aburahi” derives from the descent of the Aburahi deity upon Mount Aburahi accompanied by a light like the flame of oil. There is also a tradition that {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}} built the shrine buildings and enshrined Aburahi Daimyōjin.

The first appearance in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=national chronicles}} is in the *{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}*, under the entry for {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1st year, {{ill|December 3 (Lunisolar)|Q841033|qid=Q841033|lt=December 3}} ({{ill|878|Q23910|qid=Q23910}} {{ill|January 9|Q2238|qid=Q2238}}), which states: “Aburahi no Kami of {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}, ranked Senior Sixth Rank Upper, is granted Junior Fifth Rank Lower ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}).” There is a theory that identifies it with the “Kawakare Shrine, two seats” listed in the *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}* for {{ill|Kōka District, Shiga|Q4227244|qid=Q4227244}},<ref>*Ōmi Meiseki Annaiki*</ref> but this is difficult to accept,<ref>Uno, “Kawakare Shrine.” The same *Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku* records under {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 3rd year, {{ill|April 8 (Lunisolar)|Q839007|qid=Q839007|lt=April 8}} ({{ill|861|Q23913|qid=Q23913}} {{ill|May 21|Q2580|qid=Q2580}}): “Kawakare no Kami of Ōmi Province, Junior Fifth Rank Lower, is granted Senior Fifth Rank Lower.” Since by {{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 1st year ({{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}) it was already Senior Fifth Rank Lower, the accounts do not align.</ref>

In the main hall there is a ridge tag dated {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 2 ({{ill|1493|Q6687|qid=Q6687}}) bearing the inscription “Shōichi-i Aburahi Daimyōjin,” which clarifies the construction period. It was the foremost renowned shrine in the Kōga region, and in the medieval period the {{ill|Kōga-ryū|Q6455112|qid=Q6455112|lt=Kōga warriors}} revered {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}} as a war god and worshipped it as the “{{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}} of Kōga.”

For a long time, {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} (the syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism) was practiced, and Aburahi-ji (Kongō-ji) served as the shrine-temple. However, in the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period, with the implementation of {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, the shrine was separated from Aburahi-ji, and Aburahi-ji changed its name to Jingū-ji and became independent. Nevertheless, many Buddhist-related cultural properties remain at the shrine.

In {{ill|1906|Q2049|qid=Q2049}} (Meiji 39), the shrine was elevated to the rank of {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}}, and in {{ill|1911|Q2076|qid=Q2076}} (Meiji 44), ten shrines within the village were {{ill|Shrine Consolidation Policy|Q11590700|qid=Q11590700|lt=enshrined together}} as subordinate shrines.

=== Enshrined deities ===
* Main deity – Aburahi Ōkami
* East side hall – {{ill|Mizuhanome|lt=Mizuhanome-no-Kami|qid=Q8191796}}
* West side hall – {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Kami|qid=Q3090037}}

=== Precincts ===
* Main hall ({{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}) – Rebuilt in {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 2 ({{ill|1493|Q6687|qid=Q6687}}). Three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}}, {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}.
* Inner gate
* Worship hall (Important Cultural Property) – Rebuilt in the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531}}. {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}, gable entrance, cypress bark roofing.
* East cloister (Important Cultural Property) – Built in {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 9 ({{ill|1566|Q6638|qid=Q6638}}). Cypress bark roofing.
* West cloister (Important Cultural Property) – Built in Eiroku 9 (1566). Cypress bark roofing.
* Rōmon gate (Important Cultural Property) – Built in Eiroku 9 (1566). Irimoya-zukuri, cypress bark roofing.
* {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|qid=Q11390939}}
* {{ill|Shinmei shrines|Q11590310|qid=Q11590310}}
* {{ill|Hiyoshi Shrine|Q11505065|qid=Q11505065}}
* {{ill|Kasuga Shrines|Q10855011|qid=Q10855011}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konpira Shrine}}
* Sakura Shrine
* Tsunematsu Shrine
* Ancestral Spirit Shrine
* Former sutra repository
* Kōga Historical and Folklore Museum
* Bell tower – The hanging temple bell is designated a tangible cultural property of Kōka City. It was cast in {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} 6 ({{ill|1620|Q6810|qid=Q6810}}) by founders from {{ill|Kurita District, Shiga|Q6446084|qid=Q6446084}}, {{ill|Tsuji|Q11638251|qid=Q11638251}}, through donations by {{ill|Yamaoka Kageyori|Q11467812|qid=Q11467812}} and others. It is a remnant of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}.
* Shrine office
* Assembly hall
* Off-site shrines
** Take Shrine
** Shirahige Shrine

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Main hall, with: 15 ridge tags
* Worship hall
* Rōmon gate and cloisters, 3 structures, with: 3 ridge tags

=== National Historic Site ===
* Aburahi Shrine precincts (part of the {{ill|Kōka ikki|Q85882491|qid=Q85882491}} ruins group)

=== Nationally Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property ===
* Aburahi Taiko Dance (Aburahi Shrine Yakko-furi Taiko Dance Preservation Society)

=== Shiga Prefecture–Designated Tangible Cultural Properties ===
* Fukutayū deity mask, 1 piece, with: Zuzuiko doll, 1 figure

=== Shiga Prefecture–Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Properties ===
* Taiko dance (Aburahi Shrine Taiko Dance Preservation Society)
* {{ill|Yakko-furi|Q11446618|qid=Q11446618|lt=Yakko procession}} (Aburahi Shrine Yakko-furi Preservation Society)

=== Kōka City–Designated Tangible Cultural Properties ===
* Hanging Buddhist image group of Aburahi Shrine
* Three Thousand Seed Buddhas
* Colored silk painting of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}} illustrated biography
* Colored silk painting of the Eleven-Deity Mandala
* Colored silk painting of the {{ill|Thousand-armed Kannon|Q10904910|qid=Q10904910}} triad mandala
* Colored silk painting of the {{ill|Benzaiten|lt=Benzaiten|Q818468|qid=Q818468}} triad mandala
* Colored silk painting of the {{ill|Jūniten|Q9503981|qid=Q9503981}}
* Old masks
* Temple bell

=== Kōka City–Designated Natural Monument ===

=== Festivals ===
